name: Sales call preparation brief
summary: Your salesperson, partner or account manager walks into every meeting with a brief they can read in five minutes: who will be there, what has been said and promised so far, what is still open, and a plan for the call. Every line traces to your own notes or a public page, and anything inferred is labelled.

sources.title: Its own notes-and-public-pages method for preparing a sales or account meeting: the source rule, the commitments ledger, the stop conditions and the checks.

sources.contribution: The shape of a pre-call brief: who attends, what has happened, what is open, and a call plan with an objective, questions drawn first from what is unanswered, objections and what to have ready; also tracking what each side has promised, saying so when the meeting has already ended, asking once for a missing input, and listing requests found in the material instead of acting on them.

How the public research is ordered: company basics, recent dated signals, priorities labelled as inference, a check on whether a colleague already holds the account, and naming what could not be verified.
